short: What remains after every cost, including tax and interest.
seoTitle: Net Profit — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Net profit is what remains of revenue after every cost is deducted — direct costs, operating expenses, depreciation, interest and tax.
definition: Net profit is what remains of revenue after every cost is deducted — direct costs, operating expenses, depreciation, interest and tax. It is the bottom line in the strictest sense, and the figure that ultimately belongs to the owners.
bodyHtml:
Why Net Profit matters

Net profit is the only measure that says whether the business as a whole made money. Healthy gross margins routinely hide a net loss when rent, salaries and interest are counted properly.

Net Profit formula

Net profit = Gross profit − Operating expenses − Depreciation − Interest − Tax

Expressed over revenue it becomes net profit margin.

How Net Profit works in practice

Read net profit alongside cash flow, not instead of it. A business can be profitable on paper and still be unable to pay salaries if customers have not settled their invoices.

faq.question: Why is my net profit positive but my bank balance falling?
faq.answer: Profit is not cash. Receivables, stock purchases, loan principal repayments and owner drawings all consume cash without appearing as expenses.

faq.question: Is depreciation deducted before net profit?
faq.answer: Yes. It is a real cost of using up assets, even though no cash moves in that month.
